title: Rosemary Smith remote-views a downed Tu-22 in Zaire

tellings.quote: even Jimmy Carter is on record saying, "The craziest thing of my presidency from 1976 to 1980 was actually this woman, Rosemary Smith, finding a downed TU22 Russian cargo plane."
And she essentially made a circle on the map, and it was a 3-square-mile area, and the plane was inside that.
tellings.difference: Paul Smith tells it secondhand, credits Dale Graff, dates it to 1979 and adds the 3-square-mile circle drawn on the map.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Rosemary Smith remote-viewing the downed Tu-22 in Zaire during Carter's presidency.

as_told.title: Remote viewer locates downed Tu-22 in Zaire (Carter)

plain: During Jimmy Carter's presidency, a woman named Rosemary Smith is said to have used remote viewing, a claimed ability to see distant places with the mind alone, to find a Soviet Tu-22 plane that had crashed in Zaire, drawing a circle of about three square miles on a map that held the wreck. Carter himself is heard saying "we located the plane where she said it was," the only inexplicable thing he ever experienced, and Michels retells it on several episodes. Paul Smith, a former Army remote viewer, tells it secondhand from Dale Graff, who worked on the government's psychic spying effort, and dates it to 1979.
